title.narrative: [CONSORTIUM] Provision of integrated lifesaving responses to populations affected by displacement and famine in Kassala, New Halfa, and Gharb Kassala localities

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project, "Provision of Integrated Lifesaving Responses to Populations Affected by Displacement and Famine in Kassala, New Halfa, and Gharb Kassala Localities," addresses the critical humanitarian needs of conflict-affected populations in Eastern Sudan. With a budget of $3,382,000 it aims to deliver integrated, multi-sectoral services to 206,452 individuals, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities, and vulnerable residents. These populations are heavily impacted by displacement, food insecurity, cholera outbreaks, and limited access to essential services. The project focuses on women, children, and vulnerable populations such as persons with disability in Kassala, New Halfa, and Gharb Kassala, areas of high humanitarian need.ltbrgtHealth: The project will operate six Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) and two mobile clinics in Kassala and New Halfa, providing critical services such as maternal and child healthcare, vaccinations, disease management, and emergency referrals. Priority will be given to pregnant women and children under five. Health workers will receive infection prevention and maternal health training, while a health information system (HIS) will track service delivery and health outcomes. The project will respond to cholera, including treatment, surveillance, risk communication, and community engagement.lt/pgtltpgtNutrition: The project will combat malnutrition by implementing Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) services. (OTP) and (TSFP) will be operated at six static centers to treat and prevent severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women. Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counseling will help improve feeding practices. The project emphasizes regular screening and the distribution of micronutrient powders and fortified foods to prevent malnutrition. 7,886 beneficiaries are targeted ltbrgtWASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene): To prevent the spread of waterborne diseases such as cholera, the project will rehabilitate water systems, construct gender-responsive latrines, and promote safe hygiene practices. It will repair pipelines, rehabilitate water points, and distribute hygiene kits to vulnerable households, including jerry cans, soap, and water purification tablets. Community-led sanitation campaigns will promote awareness and reduce disease outbreaks.ltbrgtProtection: The protection component safeguards vulnerable populations, particularly women and children. The project will provide psychosocial support and case management for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) and unaccompanied minors and establish mobile safe spaces for children. It will also strengthen referral systems for GBV survivors and provide legal aid, medical support, and emergency cash assistance. Dignity kits will be distributed to women and girls, and child protection and GBV training will be offered to community networks to ensure sustainability.ltbrgtCommunity Involvement and Coordination:ltbrgtThe project will be implemented closely with the State Ministry of Health (SMOH), local authorities, and organizations such as WHO, UNICEF, and Plan International. Regular consultations with community leaders will ensure that interventions are culturally appropriate and responsive to the evolving needs of the target populations. Alight’s partnerships with SMOH, HAC, and local health authorities will ensure alignment with national priorities, promoting sustainability and local ownership.ltbrgtStrategic Alignment:ltbrgtThe project aligns with the Lifesaving response to displacement and famine and relevant cluster strategies in WASH, health, nutrition, and protection. The project aims to reduce mortality and morbidity by addressing these sectors, strengthening local capacity, and fostering safe, resilient communities. Capacity-building efforts, including training health workers and community volunteers, ensure local systems can continue addressing needs beyond the project’s duration.ltbrgtlt/pgt
